html:
José Gervasio Artigas was the leader of the revolution in the Banda Oriental, today's Uruguay, from 1811 to 1820. He is the national hero of Uruguay.

Born in Montevideo, he served as a frontier officer before joining the revolt against Spain in 1811. When Buenos Aires made a truce that handed his land back, he led much of its people on an exodus across the Uruguay River. He fought both the Spanish and the centralists of Buenos Aires, calling for a federation of free provinces, and became Protector of the League of the Free Peoples. In 1815 he decreed a land reform to give land to the poor, Indigenous and Black.

A Portuguese-Brazilian army invaded in 1816 and defeated him by 1820. He spent his last thirty years in exile in Paraguay. His ideas of federalism and his name are central to Uruguay's sense of itself.
